questions.explanation: From B to D is a minor third of three semitones, the upward span from vi to I in D major. A major second or major third misstates the distance, and a perfect fourth overcounts it.

questions.topic: The supertonic and its use in place of the subdominant
questions.stem: Explain why ii can replace IV before the dominant.

answer.exemplar: ii shares pre-dominant function with IV and leads smoothly to V, so it can substitute without changing the progression's direction.

questions.explanation: ii can replace IV before the dominant because both share pre-dominant function and lead smoothly to V. The idea that only IV can prepare V fails, since ii supplies the same directional pull.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting the diatonic chords of a passage
questions.learningObjective: Count diatonic chords in a progression
questions.stem: In a D major passage with chords D, G, A, Bm, and Em, how many are diatonic?
questions.explanation: All five chords are diatonic to D major: D, G, and A are major, while Bm and Em are minor. None is chromatic, so any smaller count wrongly excludes a legitimate diatonic chord.
